edit.description: the worktree-lock case's closing assertion establishes the loop's cardinality instead of a state zero iterations also leave

summary: The worktree-lock case's declared vacuity pin holds identically over zero iterations, so "each blocked" is three verdicts only by the array literal

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: the case's closing assertion is false when the command loop runs fewer than its three commands, so the per-command verdicts inside it cannot be inherited from a loop that fell through
pins: each git worktree add, remove and prune runs under the worktree lock
notes: Verified this tick. `tests/waitLock.test.ts:277`-`:279` closes on `expect(existsSync(wt)).toBe(false)` under a comment claiming it proves all three ran; `wt` (`:237`) is only created by the loop's own `add`, so the assertion is equally true over zero iterations. The per-command `waitFor` and `done` verdicts inside the loop are real; nothing outside it counts them.
